title: Compact compatible-family limits of finite continuous actions
statement:
Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $G$ be any topological group and let $I$ be a small nonempty partially ordered set, not assumed directed. For each $i\in I$ let $Q_i$ be a finite set with its discrete topology and a jointly continuous left $G$-action. For $i\le j$ let $r_{ji}:Q_j\to Q_i$ be $G$-equivariant maps satisfying $r_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $r_{ki}=r_{ji}\circ r_{kj}$ for $i\le j\le k$. Put $T=\prod_{i\in I}Q_i$ with product topology and
$$Q=\{z\in T:r_{ji}(z_j)=z_i\text{ for all }i\le j\}$$
with subspace topology. The space $T$ is compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected, the compatibility subset $Q$ is closed in $T$, and $Q$ is compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected. The formulas $(gz)_i=gz_i$ define a jointly continuous left $G$-action on $Q$, and every projection $Q\to Q_i$ is continuous and equivariant. Empty stages and an empty compatible-family space are permitted, and no transition map is assumed surjective.

proof.text: Every $Q_i$ is quasi-compact: from an open cover choose one member per point, giving a finite subcover (empty if $Q_i$ is empty). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tychonoff-product-quasi-compact] to this small family. Thus $T$ is quasi-compact.

For $a\in Q_i$, the cylinder $C_{i,a}=\{z:z_i=a\}$ is open; its complement is the union of the other $i$-coordinate cylinders, so it is closed too. Distinct tuples differ at some $i$ and are separated by $C_{i,a}$ and its complement. These sets also separate any subset containing those tuples, making it disconnected. Hence $T$ is Hausdorff and totally disconnected. Intersecting these cylinders with $Q$ proves the same two properties for its subspace topology.

source.place: Tag 08ZY, lemma-profinite, proof of (1) implies (2): distinct-coordinate separation, written out for the product and its subspace.

proof.text: If $z\notin Q$, choose $i\le j$ with $r_{ji}(z_j)\ne z_i$. The open cylinder fixing coordinates $i,j$ to $z_i,z_j$ contains $z$ and is disjoint from $Q$. Thus $T\setminus Q$ is open and $Q$ is closed. This argument requires neither directedness nor surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 08ZV, lemma-inverse-limit-quasi-compact: closedness of the compatibility locus; direct discrete-cylinder argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact] with $X=T$ and $E=Q$, using step 1 and step 3. It gives quasi-compactness of $Q$ in exactly the induced topology. Together with step 2, $T$ and $Q$ are compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected.

source.place: Tag 005C, lemma-closed-in-quasi-compact; applied as in Tag 08ZV.

proof.text: For $z\in Q$, equivariance gives $r_{ji}(gz_j)=g r_{ji}(z_j)=gz_i$, so coordinatewise action preserves $Q$. The identities $(1z)_i=z_i$ and $((gh)z)_i=g(hz_i)$ prove the action laws by equality of coordinates. The projection $p_i(z)=z_i$ is equivariant because $p_i(gz)=gz_i=g p_i(z)$.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, p. 28; agent expansion of the coordinatewise action on pro-objects in finite discrete G-sets.

proof.text: Each $p_i$ is continuous since $p_i^{-1}(U)=Q\cap\pi_i^{-1}(U)$ is open for open $U\subseteq Q_i$. The map $b_i:G\times Q\to G\times Q_i$, $(g,z)\mapsto(g,p_i(z))$, is continuous: inverse images of open rectangles are $V\times p_i^{-1}(U)$. Write $a_i$ for the given jointly continuous stage action and $a$ for step 5. Then $a^{-1}(p_i^{-1}(U))=b_i^{-1}(a_i^{-1}(U))$ is open. Finite intersections and unions of the sets $p_i^{-1}(U)$ give every open of $Q$, by the product and subspace definitions. Therefore $a$ is jointly continuous, also when $Q$ is empty.
